notes.description: Why not (fully) measured, or what was dropped.

reason.description: Why this one, as shown and recorded.

BugOutcome.description: The bug's outcome; distinct from a task's verdict.

BugReport.description:
A bug: where it lives, the person's triad, the reproductions and how
far it got. The `bug` payload, and what speccoder keeps of it.

acceptance.description: What the fix's acceptance set came from.

code.description: The code of the last stop or refusal.

confirm_digest.description: The digest waiting for the person's confirmation.

handoff.description: The engine's hand-off, when it stopped.

held_out.description: The held-out variants (never their content or path).

pass_to_pass.description: The tests selected to stay green.

recorded_commit.description: The planning commit that recorded it.

unit.description: The unit, as the adapter names it (`007-bugfixes`, `bugs/<slug>`).

oneOf.description: The triad is being recorded.
Reproductions are being written and shown to fail.
The reproductions wait for the person's confirmation.
The pass-to-pass set is chosen and run.
The fix is attempted and judged.
The verdict commit.

Candidate.description: Someone else's fix, judged as the attempt.

applied.description: It was applied as the attempt.

origin.description: A patch or a pull request.

CandidateOrigin.description: Where a foreign fix came from.

oneOf.description: A patch file.
A GitHub pull request.

paths.description: The judge paths it touches, or the hunks that did not apply.

exit_code.description: Process exit code, if it exited.

flaky.description:
It failed once and passed when run again: named, never trusted as
task evidence.

junit.description: Whether the check declares a JUnit report.

note.description: Why the check was skipped, errored, or has no tests.

tests.description: Tests from the JUnit report, if one was declared and freshly written.

oneOf.description: Exited 0.
Exited non-zero.
Killed at its deadline.
Not applicable (its `when_exists` path is absent); not evidence of anything.
Could not be run at all (e.g. command not found).

Comparison.description: What changed relative to a baseline (pass-to-pass).

failing_as_before.description: Checks failing now only because of tests that already failed in the baseline.

regressions.description: Tests that passed in the baseline and now fail or are missing.

Confirmation.description: The person's one confirmation, bound to what they saw.

digest.description:
`sha256:<hex>` over the reproductions shown (their files and
statement ids).

triad_digest.description: The triad's digest when confirmed: a different one lapses this.

commit.description: The commit on `speccoder/<feature>` holding the appended section.

hooks.description: Extension hooks run, offered or skipped around it.

unrequested.description: `unrequested` findings: for a person, never turned into tasks.

Counts.description: Rejected of judged, for one source.

discarded.description: Paths the previous attempt changed; its changes were discarded.

digest.description: What the next attempt was told.

run_id.description: The agentplane run of the attempt.

FailedCheck.description: One check that did not pass.

excerpt.description: Output from the first error line on, capped.

failing_tests.description: Failing test IDs, when the check reports tests.

FinalState.description: A reproduction on the final tree.

oneOf.description: It passed.
It failed.
Not run (no attempt yet).

note.description: Why nothing ran, or the record could not be written.

oneOf.description: No `min_strength`.
Met at once.
Met after one regeneration of the acceptance tests.
Not met, or not measurable.

Handoff.description:
The hand-off of a stopped bug, composed by the engine from the journal
(never written by a model).

claim.description: The author's last words, labelled as its claim.

HeldOutVariant.description: A held-out variant, as the payload shows it: never its content or path.

HomeKind.description: Where the format keeps the bug.

OpenSpec: the standing bug-fix change.

InstructionFile.description: A repository instructions file given to an attempt.

cut.description: Cut to fit the instructions budget.

IssueRef.description: The issue a bug was recorded from.

context_digest.description:
The digest of its context-manifest entry (title and body as given
to the reproduction author).

MemberFinal.description: A pass-to-pass member on the final tree.

oneOf.description: Passed, by name.
Failed.
Not found in the final run: a failure.
Not run yet.

survivors.description: The missed ones, as the tool names them.

combined.description: Against the visible and the held-out set together.

rationale.description: What it gets wrong, in one line (the author's claim).

scenario.description: The scenario or requirement it gets wrong.

NextStep.description: One step a person can take.

command.description: A copy-pasteable command (`"…"` marks text the person writes).

It did not build or the tests could not be collected: not judged.

PassToPass.description: The tests that passed before the fix and must pass after it.

PassToPassMember.description: One test that must stay green.

test.description: The test id, as the runner reports it.

PassToPassState.description: Whether anything was selected for pass-to-pass.

oneOf.description: Members were selected.
Nothing was: never counted as passed.

Permitted.description: An alternative the author says the spec allows.

digest.description: `sha256:<hex>` of its files: what a ruling is bound to.

failing.description: The failing run's last lines, when rejected.

outcome.description: Against the visible and held-out set together.

patch.description: Where its patch is kept for a person.

rationale.description: The freedom it uses (the author's claim).

scenario.description: The scenario whose open choice it takes differently.

The set rejects it on an assertion: probably over-strict.
Rejected, and a person ruled the tests right.
Timed out: no finding (a hang is not an assertion).
Did not build: no finding.

PreFrozenRef.description: Where the confirmed reproductions are kept, as recorded with the fix.

RedClass.description:
What a red run of acceptance tests showed.

Only [`RedClass::Assertion`] and [`RedClass::Absent`] are red: a test was
collected and failed on an assertion, or the tests could not build only
because symbols the task is to introduce do not exist yet. Everything
else is not demonstrated.

oneOf.description: A collected test failed on an assertion.
The only build or import errors name symbols that do not exist yet.
Any other build error.
Tests errored at setup or collection.
The run hit its deadline.
Nothing was collected.
Red once, not red when confirmed.
The output was not recognised.
The tests passed.

Regression.description: A test that passed in the baseline and no longer does.

Rejection.description:
The person rejected the reproductions shown; the reason goes to the
author's next try.

ReproduceTry.description: One try of the reproduction author.

discarded.description: Why the whole try was discarded (`wrote outside tests`, …).

rejection.description: The person's reason for rejecting the reproductions before it.

argv.description: The command that runs only it.

baseline.description: Its class on the untouched code, run twice.

statement.description:
The statement it reproduces (`E1`) — or, for a test of an
*Unchanged* statement, that one (`U1`).

oneOf.description: The test-blind reproduction author.
The person (`--test`).

RevertOutcome.description: A reproduction against the revert candidate (the fix undone).

oneOf.description: It failed on an assertion: it tells the fix from no fix.
It passed without the fix.
The revert did not build: no evidence either way.
Not run.

outcome.description: The gravest outcome over the reproductions.

rejected_by.description: The statements whose reproduction failed on an assertion.

Ruling.description:
A person's ruling that an over-strict finding was wrong: the tests were
right, the alternative is not what the spec allows.

RunMode.description: How a run started from the review asks for a person.

oneOf.description:
*Ask on Risky Calls*: a call the policy asks about is asked inline,
as a run from the interface does.

*Autopilot*: nothing asks; a call the policy would ask about and no
ticked grant covers is refused for the run and listed afterwards.

acceptance.description: Spec-derived acceptance tests: files, command, red/green, notes.

attestation.description:
What the tick's attestation came to: `{ state: signed | unsigned |
missing, signer, reason }`.

bug.description:
A bug task: the bug as this run left it (reproduce, confirm, the
fix's discrimination).

commit.description: The commit on `speccoder/<feature>` holding the attempt and the tick.

earlier.description: Earlier attempts at this task in this run, discarded and retried.

instructions.description:
The repository's instructions the attempt was given (`AGENTS.md`,
`CLAUDE.md`, …), root first.

integrity.description: Integrity findings of the attempt's diff (each also fails the verdict).

model_report.description: The model's own closing report — its claim, not the verdict.

monitor.description:
The gaming monitor's view of a passing attempt: `suspected`,
`findings`, `usage` (or `error`). Never shown to the implementer.

mutation.description:
Mutation testing of the attempt's changes: `tool`, `caught`,
`missed`, `timeout`, `unviable`, `survivors` (or `error`).

notices.description: Things a person should know that are not part of the verdict.

pending.description: The call awaiting approval, if any.

reason.description: Why the attempt stopped, when it did not complete.

retry_stop.description: Why no further attempt was made after a failed one, if it failed.

run_id.description: The agentplane run of the attempt.

samples.description: Best-of-n: every sample's evidence and which one was kept.

saved_attempt.description:
The ref this attempt was saved under when it did not pass; the
worktree went back to where it started.

scope.description: Changes outside the paths the task names: reported, never gated.

set_aside.description: The ref uncommitted leftovers were saved under before this run.

strength.description: The acceptance set's strength: after a `verified` verdict.

ticked.description: The engine ticked the task in the worktree's `tasks.md`.

tool_calls.description: Every tool call with the policy's decision.

usage.description: Token usage summed over the attempt's turns.

verdict.description: The verifier's verdict (only for completed attempts).

verification.description: Checks after the attempt, compared with the baseline.

worktree.description: The worktree the attempt worked in.

ScopeFinding.description: What an attempt changed beyond the paths its task names.

stated.description: The task names at least one path.

SealedRef.description: A sealed held-out set: kept in the state directory, never shown.

key.description: The requirement it is keyed by.

SpecialCase.description:
One special-case candidate: a fix that recognises a reproduction's
literal inputs.

digest.description: `sha256:<hex>` of its files: what a ruling is bound to.

regenerated.description: Its statement's held-out variant was written again once, told it.

rejected.description: The combined set (reproductions and held-out variants) rejected it.

ruled.description: A person ruled the tests right about it.

statement.description: The statement whose reproduction it targets.

oneOf.description: Everything planned was run.
The budget ran out: what ran is recorded.
Nothing could be judged (no tool, no variant, an error).
The change touches no source file.

Statement.description: One statement of the triad, in the person's words.

StatementsShown.description: Statements, by what the tries showed.

reproduced.description: Red by assertion in some try.

share.description: Rejected / judged over every source; `None` when nothing was judged.

survivors.description: What got through: mutant names and near-miss ids with their scenario.

TestOutcome.description: Outcome of one test from a JUnit report.

oneOf.description: Passed.
Failed (an assertion, a `<failure>` in JUnit).
Skipped or ignored.

Errored before or outside an assertion (a `<error>` in JUnit: setup,
collection, an unexpected exception).

digest.description:
`sha256:<hex>` over the normalised statements: a different digest
lapses a confirmation.

expected.description: What should happen instead; at least one.

unchanged.description: What must keep working as it does.

TryStatement.description: One statement's class in one try.

class.description:
What its test did on the untouched code (`assertion` only when both
runs failed on one).

excerpt.description: Up to 20 lines of the run, when it was not red.

Verdict.description: How strong the evidence for a task is.

oneOf.description: A task-specific check produced evidence, nothing failed, nothing regressed.
Nothing failed or regressed, but nothing task-specific was established.
Something failed or regressed.

checks.description: One result per configured check, in configuration order.

comparison.description: Comparison with a baseline, if one was given.

root.description: Project root the checks ran in.

The interface a person acted through, as a write records it (`via`):
one vocabulary for every record. Records written before it named
`cli`, `tui` or `dashboard` (read as [`Via::Terminal`]) and
`editor <name>` (read as [`Via::Acp`], the name a separate client).

oneOf.description: A terminal: the line CLI, its prompts, the dashboard.
The web app, in a browser tab or the desktop window.
The desktop window, once it can tell itself from a tab.
An editor over the Agent Client Protocol.
A phone.
Continuous integration.
A client over the Model Context Protocol.
